intro.name: The beginning
intro.text:
The artists of Isola assemble beneath the shade of broad tropical leaves. There are bowls of crushed berry pigments, charcoal sticks, colored earth, barkcloth, smooth wood, and prepared leaves. A row of judges sits before a growing collection of drawings. (Artist) has entered the competition, although (artist.he/she) has not yet decided what to draw.
An enthusiastic organizer announces, "May the finest artist win!" From the back, someone mutters, "May the judges know what art is."
WHAT SHOULD (ARTIST) DRAW?

choices.label: A PORTRAIT OF A FELLOW VILLAGER

a1.text: The Island in a Single Picture: The drawing captures the reefs, palms, and distant hills so beautifully that even the judges fall silent. (Artist) wins.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has an Artistic skill

a2.text: The Rain's Contribution: A tropical shower washes the pigments into dramatic streaks. (Artist) calls the result "The Storm." One judge loves it; another calls it an accident.

a3.text:
The Accidental Map: An explorer recognizes a detail that resembles a little-known route through the island.
the contest result is disputed.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has exploration progress

a4.text: The Wrong Island: (Artist) paints a magnificent beach but places the waterfall on the wrong side. The judges praise the technique while the audience laughs at the geography.

b1.text: A Living Likeness: The subject is moved by the careful portrait. (Artist) receives first prize.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has an Artistic skill

b2.text: The Nose Controversy: (Sitter), the subject, objects that (sitter.his/her) nose looks enormous. (Artist) insists the likeness is accurate. The village debates whether accuracy is always kind.

b4.text: The Unexpected Friendship: A portrait of a lonely villager prompts a warm conversation. The prize is modest, but both villagers gain friendship.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has an Artistic skill

c1.text: The Visionary: A striking imagined landscape astonishes the judges. (Artist) earns a special prize for creativity.

c2.text: The Unidentifiable Thing: The judges cannot agree whether the drawing depicts a fish, a bird, or a coconut with legs. The children adore it.

c3.text: The Picture That Changed: At sunset the image seems subtly different. A scholar blames shifting light; a mystic disagrees.

c4.text: The Storyteller: The picture inspires an improvised tale that captivates the audience.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has an Artistic skill

d1.text: A New Pigment: (Artist) finds a way to make a more durable color from island materials.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has an Artistic skill

d2.text: The Beautiful Disaster: The colors run together into a muddy smear. A judge politely describes it as "energetic." (Artist) receives no prize and a little embarrassment.

d3.text: The Pattern of Light: Layered pigments produce a remarkable effect in the afternoon sun.

text_only.reason: rule 8: no game has an Artistic skill

d4.text: The Great Copying Scandal: Another contestant claims (Artist) stole a design. A fair inquiry clears (Artist), reveals shared inspiration, or uncovers deliberate copying.

coda_child.text: A child's simple drawing of the village may defeat every adult entry. The result is celebrated, disputed, or taken as a reminder that art need not be complicated.
